::: {.lede}
I am an architect who moved into urban climate modelling through computational
fluid dynamics. Architectural practice takes a great deal for granted, and the
assumptions buried in its comfort models are what I have been chasing upward in
scale ever since — from a room, to a building, to a city.
:::

I build the mesoscale-to-microscale chain at [iFOREST](https://iforest.global/)
in Delhi: WRF compiled and run from scratch on cloud HPC for two Indian cities,
driving PALM-4U for interventions in the existing urban fabric and City Energy
Analyst for building energy response. Before that, an M.Tech in Geoinformatics
at CSRE, IIT Bombay, and CFD and low-cost particulate sensing at the Royal
Danish Academy, Copenhagen.

What holds these together is validation. A microclimate model becomes a claim
about people the moment anyone acts on it, so the work I keep is the work that
carries its own error record — station comparisons, per-class classifier
attribution, and a statement of where the method fails. One current thread is
documenting where the 2012 Local Climate Zone typology does not describe the
urban form of Indian cities.
